headline: Burnham to force employers to publish salaries on job ads in latest government ‘small fix’ – UK politics live

members.title: Say what you pay: employers to be forced to put salaries on job ads, says Burnham
members.lead: Workers’ rights campaigners say measure will help young people and women in particular achieve more equal pay Business live – latest updates Employers will be forced to publish salaries on job adverts, Andy Burnham has announced, in an effort to empower both employees and jobseekers. The prime minister said his government would bring in a legal requirement for companies to say what they pay when listing new jobs, which campaigners say will help young people and women in particular achieve more equal pay. members.title: Burnham to force employers to publish salaries on job ads in latest government ‘small fix’ – UK politics live
members.lead: Prime minister said his government would bring in legal requirement for companies to say what they pay when listing new jobs Shabana Mahmood has signalled she is considering a change to knife laws, following the murder of Henry Nowak. The Home Secretary said she had not “taken any options off the table”, after Nowak’s father, Mark Nowak, called for a clearer definition in law of what a Sikh kirpan looks like. I haven’t taken any options off the table. I’m also not going in with a fixed mind about what the right clarifications of the law might be. It’s important to get the right balance between religious expression in this country, which is something that many of us of a faith, including myself, hold very dearly, but do so in a way that is within what we expect of our citizens for the purposes of the criminal law. Whether you’re a young person starting out or a parent trying to support your family, you should know what a job pays before spending your time and effort applying for it. That’s why we will make it a legal requirement for all employers to say what you pay. Continue reading...
